summary: Computes time-phase subdivisions from the input value *a2 (0.0, *a2-3.5999999, *a2*0.5, *a2*0.25, *a2*0.75) into a local phase array, then distributes them to per-element sub-structures via RangeProportionInitializer. The outer loop walks this[3] elements starting at this[4] with a 120-byte stride; each element holds a 28-byte-stride sub-element array whose count lives at element+112. For each sub-element it reads a phase index at sub+24, computes target = sub[4] - sub[3] + phase[index], and calls RangeProportionInitializer(sub, phase[index], target). Returns the number of elements iterated. Prior analysis ties this to PitStopOperationTimer-driven multi-channel animation timing.

Compute the offset phase value *a2 - 3.5999999 and store it into the local phase array at v18[14].
Derive proportional phases from *a2: v19 = v22 = *a2 * 0.5, v21 = *a2 * 0.25, v23 = *a2 * 0.75.
Outer guard: only enter the element loop when the element count this[3] (this+0xC) is greater than zero.
Outer loop over this[3] elements, base pointer this[4] (this+0x10), advancing by a 120-byte stride each iteration.
Inner guard: only process sub-elements when the per-element count at element+112 is greater than zero.
Inner loop over the 28-byte-stride sub-elements of each 120-byte element, bounded by the count at element+112.
For each sub-element: read the phase index v13 from sub+24, then compute target v16 = sub[4] - sub[3] + phase[v13].
Call RangeProportionInitializer(sub, phase[v13], v16) to assign the range/proportion values onto the sub-element for animation tweening.
Return result, the number of elements iterated (incremented once per outer-loop iteration).
